# Sirach Chapter 48 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Sirach 48 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/SIR_048_page_001.jpg

---

48:1 And Elijah arose like a fire, and his word burned like a torch.

48:2 He brought a famine upon them, and by his zeal he reduced their number.

48:3 By the word of the Lord he shut up the heaven, and thus three times brought down fire.

48:4 How glorified you were, Elijah, in your wondrous deeds! And who has the right to boast, as you have?

48:5 You who raised a dead man from death and from Hades by the word of the Most High;

48:6 who brought kings down to destruction, and men of honor from their beds;

48:7 who heard rebuke at Sinai and judgments of vengeance at Horeb;

48:8 who anointed kings as avengers and prophets as successors after him;

48:9 who was taken up in a whirlwind of fire, in a chariot with horses of fire;

48:10 who is appointed in the judgments to calm the wrath before it burns hot, to turn the heart of the father to the son, and to restore the tribes of Jacob.

48:11 Blessed are those who see you and those who fall asleep in love, for we also shall surely live.

48:12 Elijah was wrapped in the whirlwind, and Elisha was filled with his spirit; in all his days he was not shaken by any ruler, and no one made him subject.

48:13 Nothing was too hard for him, and from wherever he had lain, his body prophesied.

48:14 In his life he worked wonders, and in his death his deeds were marvelous.

48:15 Despite all this, the people did not repent, and they did not turn away from their sins, until they were carried off as plunder from their land and were scattered through all the earth.

48:16 A very small people were left over, and a ruler from the house of David; some of them did what was pleasing to God, and some multiplied sins.

48:17 Hezekiah strengthened his city and brought water into its midst; he bored through the rock with iron tools and dammed up springs with wells.

48:18 In his days Sennacherib came up and sent Rabshakeh and departed; he lifted up his hand against Zion and boasted in his arrogance.

48:19 Then their hearts were shaken and their hands trembled, and they were in anguish like women in labor.

48:20 And they called upon the merciful Lord and spread out their hands to him; and the Holy One quickly heard them from heaven and delivered them by the hand of Isaiah.

48:21 He struck the camp of the Assyrians, and his messenger destroyed them.

48:22 For Hezekiah did what was good and walked firmly in the ways of David his father, as Isaiah the prophet had commanded him, the great prophet who was faithful in his vision.

48:23 In his days the sun went backward, and he added years to the king's life.

48:24 By a great spirit he saw the last things, and comforted those who mourned in Zion.

48:25 He revealed things to come until the end of time, and hidden things before they came to pass.
